80407.subject: Why Job Hopping Is Losing Its Payoff
80407.body:
Forbes Edge

Автор: Forbes


Автор: Forbes

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/why-job-hopping-losing-its-payoff-forbes-magazine-mesxc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BAxJ%2FVONFSbGRY9CXnJm0Fg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3347ze0b2yAIs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~muy7rs3o~mn-null-null&eid=fz96fz-muy7rs3o-mn
  
For ages, job hopping early in a career has been one of the ways new workers have achieved income gains, setting them on a path to higher lifetime earnings. Historically, workers see their fastest real wage growth before they hit age 35, with gains leveling off until 45 and real wages pretty much flat after that. But in a stagnant job market where employers have the upper hand, workers these days are far less likely to job hop—and those who do are seeing less substantial pay gains.  I looked into why this is a particular problem for Gen Z workers, who are trying to gain their footing in the labor market, and for younger millennials who should be in the middle of their peak earning years. According to Nela Richardson, chief economist for ADP Research, if a young worker today has “a sibling that is three or four years ahead and who entered the labor market in the Great Resignation, they’re having a completely different experience now than their older sister or brother did.’’  When comparing the stats for workers who job hop these days, compared to those who did so during the Great Resignation era, data shows that in the year ended March 2023, job switchers’ median pay grew 7.7%, a healthy 2.7% above the 5% inflation rate during that period. Meanwhile, during the 12 months ended in August 2026, the median pay of job switchers rose 4.4%, just 1% above inflation. To add further insult to injury, workers received just 52.8% of nonfarm business output as pay in the second quarter of 2026, the lowest since the Bureau of Labor Statistics started tracking this data in 1947. Experts explain that in the current labor market, employers have no need to offer premiums to lure job hoppers—or, for that matter, big raises to keep people from hopping. And in an era where ghost jobs (listed openings employers don’t really intend to fill) are on the rise and resumes are screened by AI, the hassle of job hunting isn’t necessarily worth the reward. “When we look at Glassdoor reviews, workers are constantly talking about how they feel stuck in their current jobs, and that means workers are getting more frustrated and more anxious,” says Glassdoor Chief Economist Daniel Zhao. “In a hotter job market, there would be a natural outlet for that frustration where workers would be able to hit the open market and find a better job, whether that means better career opportunities, higher wage

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk-off returns: an oil spike on Iranian tanker attacks dragged Bitcoin below $84K and flushed leveraged longs, while Coinbase, Robinhood and OKX kept building for the long game. 📉 Bitcoin Slips Below $84K as Oil Spikes on Iranian Tanker Attacks Bitcoin fell as low as about $83,840 early Wednesday after Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, pushing Brent above $101 and lifting the dollar and the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.31%. Ether lost roughly 3.5% and DOGE about 5%, with crypto liquidations climbing past $540 million. Traders now await minutes from the Fed's September meeting, due later today. Read full story 🏛️ Coinbase Revives Coinbase Pro and Launches Coinbase Global Exchange Coinbase completed its Deribit integration, creating Coinbase Global Exchange and, for the first time, linking U.S. and international crypto derivatives into a single liquidity pool under CFTC guidance. Deribit-powered options, spot margin of up to 10x on major assets and unified portfolios roll out in the coming weeks, while a rebuilt Coinbase Pro returns by year-end for spot, futures, perps, options and equities. More details 🤝 OKX Raises From Standard Chartered, Circle and Ripple at $25B Valuation OKX secured fresh investment from Circle, Ripple, quant firm Qube Research and Technologies and Standard Chartered's SC Ventures at a $25 billion pre-money valuation, extending ICE's March deal. The exchange is repositioning as a global fintech platform, and its joint venture with the NYSE owner has filed to offer 24/7 trading in tokenized shares of 63 U.S. companies settled in stablecoins. See details 🟢 Robinhood Adds $25 Million in Bitcoin to Its Balance Sheet Robinhood has bought $25 million worth of BTC, SVP Johann Kerbrat told The Block, framing it as a signal of alignment with the crypto community rather than a move that changes the trajectory of the roughly $100 billion company. The purchase lands as Robinhood readies U.S. perpetual futures and its Robinhood Chain layer 2 tops $1 billion in total value locked. Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our senior editors. America is a scientific superpower and a wellspring of new products, techniques and business models. But does it rank at the top of the innovation league table? And has President Donald Trump hurt or helped its standing? His administration has championed cutting-edge industries like semiconductors, fintech and artificial intelligence (“Whoever wins AI, WINS!”). But he has also attacked the country’s leading universities, restricted skilled immigration and cut funding to public institutions like the National Science Foundation. The Global Innovation Index ranks countries around the world based on a variety of indicators, from patents and venture-capital deals to scientific publications and school test scores. The latest index, published by the World Intellectual Property Organisation, draws partly on data from Mr Trump’s first year back in office. Has America climbed up or tumbled down the league table? And which countries are breathing down its neck? You can find out by reading the full story.
